subject: Exhibit F: Capacity uplift + billing alignment — redline coordination
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: BrightPath Procurement <procurement@brightpath.ai>, James O'Neill <james@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit F: Capacity uplift + billing alignment — redline coordination

Hi Maya / James,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, we can add the 1.5x capacity uplift for Q4 but need to align on billing proration and acceptance gates in Exhibit F so there are no surprises at invoice time. I attached a redline of Exhibit F (redline_exhibitF_v2.pdf) that: 
- adds a "Q4 uplift" SKU with a temporary throughput multiplier;
- proposes a 30-day proration window and one-off implementation credit; and
- adds an acceptance criteria subsection (performance within agreed latency targets).

Can you confirm (1) whether procurement is fine with the 30-day proration approach, and (2) whether BrightPath needs a separate PO or an SOW amendment? If you prefer, we can convert this to a change order instead of amending the Order Form.

Proposed near-term next steps:
- BrightPath to confirm billing preference (change order vs. SOW amendment) by end of week.
- Redwood to run final cost calc and share a simple invoice preview (I will loop Rishi).
- Legal to run redline and propose MSA cross-references (cc'ing Laura).

Attachments: redline_exhibitF_v2.pdf (marked), proposed-billing-proration.xlsx (calc - draft)

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Maya Desai <maya@brightpath.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: James O'Neill <james@brightpath.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exhibit F: Capacity uplift + billing alignment — redline coordination

Hi Stephanie,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the redline. We have two immediate asks from procurement/legal: 
1) We need a clear cost breakdown showing the baseline, uplift units, and the credit you mentioned — please send a sample invoice layout.
2) Our legal team flagged the proposed language in Exhibit F, section 2.3 (temporary throughput multiplier). They prefer a defined end date and a hard cap on peak usage to avoid runaway charges.

I've attached our procurement questionnaire with a few validators and the commercial team's preferred PO workflow (brightpath_procurement_qs.pdf). We can accept a change order if Redwood confirms the invoice format and adds explicit usage caps.

On timing: if Redwood can provide the invoice preview and final redline by Thursday EOD we can route for internal approval next Monday.

Thanks,
Maya Desai
VP, Platform Partnerships | BrightPath Health
maya@brightpath.ai | (617) 555-4321

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Desai <maya@brightpath.ai>, BrightPath Procurement <procurement@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exhibit F: Capacity uplift + billing alignment — redline coordination

Maya — perfect, thank you.

Rishi and Karthik will produce the invoice preview (I attached the draft calc as proposed-billing-proration.xlsx). For the legal piece: we intentionally left the uplift window open for a business-day alignment, but happy to add a firm end date and a peak cap. Two quick clarifications before Laura/Legal dive in: 
- Do you want the cap expressed as absolute throughput (e.g., 2M tokens/day) or as a % over baseline?
- For the end date, do you prefer a fixed date (we suggested 2027-12-31) or an "until further notice" clause with a 30-day termination notice?

If you confirm those two items, we'll incorporate into the next redline and Rishi will run final numbers. Suggested next step: "change order" flow with the same MSA cross-references — that seems faster for procurement signoff.

Best,
Stephanie

Attachments: proposed-billing-proration.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Exhibit F: Capacity uplift + billing alignment — redline coordination

Laura—quick forward. Can you review the attached redline and advise whether the following language is acceptable from MSA perspective? I pasted the external ask below.

> "Temporary throughput multiplier will be in effect until 2027-12-31 and capped at 150% of baseline daily throughput. Pricing will be prorated over a 30-day billing window."

Is a cap expressed as a % ok, or should we require absolute units? Also, BrightPath requested a one-off implementation credit — we proposed $12,000 in the calc. Need legal to confirm we can commit to that in a change order and whether we should add a short clawback clause if usage materially diverges.

Attachment: proposed-billing-proration.xlsx (calc)

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Director | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Desai <maya@brightpath.ai>, James O'Neill <james@brightpath.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exhibit F: Capacity uplift + billing alignment — redline coordination

Rishi / team — reviewed and added inline suggestions. High-level:

- Percent caps are acceptable for temporary uplifts but we should add a backstop in absolute units to avoid ambiguity. Suggested language: "capped at 150% of baseline daily throughput, not to exceed 2,500,000 tokens/day."
- Fix the end date to 2027-12-31 in the change order and include an automatic review 14 days before expiry to determine extension terms.
- For the $12,000 implementation credit: acceptable, but add a one-time clawback if BrightPath reduces baseline committed capacity by more than 30% within 90 days of the credit issuance.
- Add acceptance criteria reference to Exhibit A (performance SLA) rather than embedding new acceptance language in Exhibit F — keeps change order smaller.

I'll attach a marked-up change-order snippet and a short paragraph for the DocuSign cover letter. If BrightPath confirms the absolute cap and the billing flow, we can prepare the change order (not an MSA amendment) and route for signature.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
